newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firm as LME tightness draws near.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firm as LME tightness draws near.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer after a choppy session with the market recovering from a move lower mid-session.
Traders said there was some concern about the tightness on LME between the end of January and into the first week of February.
"There is some squeeze there. Some of the merchants and speculators who have positions there are beginning to pinch," said Fred Demler of E D and F Man International.
March COMEX settled 1.05 cents firmer at 107.30 cents per pound, traded 107.40 to 106.00 cents. Spot January went out 1.45 cents higher at 111.25 cents, just off the high of 111.35 cents.
A sizeable quantity of buy stops were thought to be lurking at around 108.00 cents basis March.
Volume was estimated at 8,000 lots compared to Tuesday's official 9,015 lots.
COMEX stocks fell 339 short tons Wednesday to 20,184 tons.

Meanwhile, rumors swirled concerning an Asian trading house facing possible margin call payment difficulties after granting a huge volume of LME copper and aluminum options as part of a financing operation.

"It creates some nervousness," a broker said. He believed the clearing house and exchange authorities have looked into the matter. "But following Sumitomo, any kind of hint of a trading problem gets blown up."
Construction starts on new homes in the United States slowed sharply during December to their weakest rate in 1-1/2 years according to Commerce Dept figures released Wednesday.
Starts in December fell 12.2 percent to an annual rate of 1.329 million, the lowest figure since June 1995. House and apartment construction is a key copper consuming sector.
However, total housing starts in 1996 at 1.474 million was the best since 1988.
